_meta.en: UI glossary, English to Vietnamese, for a US nail-salon pay-records app
_meta.vi: Bảng từ vựng giao diện Anh-Việt cho ứng dụng tính lương tiệm nail ở Mỹ
_meta.note: Register: Vietnamese as spoken in US nail salons (Southern-leaning, heavy English loanwords: tip, check, cash, overtime, turn, PIN, gel). Where salon slang differs from formal Vietnamese the note says so. Keep US number/date formats ($1,234.56, 10/07/2026) even in the Vietnamese UI. Keys are grouped by prefix: app, clock, ticket, pay, stmt, audit, settings, svc, day, month.

app.sign_in.note: Standard. Owners also say 'log in' in English.

app.settings.note: Standard; 'Thiết lập' is more formal and less used.

app.cancel.note: Standard. 'Hủy bỏ' is longer; keep 'Hủy' on buttons.

app.next.note: Short form of 'Tiếp theo' for buttons.

app.this_week.note: Standard; salon people say exactly this when talking about pay.

app.offline_queued.en: No connection. Saved on this tablet; will sync later.
app.offline_queued.vi: Mất mạng. Đã lưu trên máy, sẽ tự đồng bộ sau.
app.offline_queued.note: 'Mất mạng' (lost the network) is how everyone says Wi-Fi is down. 'Máy' = this device.

app.error_generic.vi: Có lỗi xảy ra. Thử lại.

app.owner.note: 'Chủ' alone is used in speech ('hỏi chủ'); 'Chủ tiệm' is clearer on screen.

app.front_desk.note: Salon slang: 'đứng quầy' (to work the counter), 'người đứng quầy' for the receptionist. Formal: 'lễ tân'.

app.bookkeeper.note: Owners say 'kế toán' or 'CPA' or 'người làm thuế'; 'kế toán' covers all three here.

clock.enter_pin.note: 'PIN' is said in English. 'Mã số' also understood.

clock.clock_in.note: Formal term is 'chấm công vào'. 'Vào ca' (start shift) is what techs say; 'bấm giờ vô' also heard in the South. Use 'Vào ca' on the button, 'chấm công' as the feature name.

clock.clock_out.note: Pairs with 'Vào ca'. Formal: 'chấm công ra'.

clock.time_clock.note: 'Chấm công' is the standard noun for attendance tracking and is understood by all.

clock.start_break.note: Salon speech: 'đi ăn' (go eat) for the lunch break; 'nghỉ' is the neutral word.

clock.clocked_in_since.note: Use 'bạn' (neutral you). Avoid 'anh/chị' because the tablet does not know gender or age.

clock.take_photo.note: Southern/US-Vietnamese say 'chụp hình'; Northern 'chụp ảnh'. Use 'hình'.

clock.pin_locked.en: Too many tries. Ask the owner.
clock.pin_locked.vi: Nhập sai nhiều lần. Hỏi chủ tiệm.
clock.pin_locked.note: 'Hỏi chủ' is the natural instruction in a salon.

clock.forgot_clock_out_fix.en: Enter the time you actually left
clock.forgot_clock_out_fix.vi: Nhập giờ bạn về thật sự
clock.forgot_clock_out_fix.note: 'Về' (go home) is how techs describe leaving.

clock.who_are_you.note: Used above a technician picker as a fallback to PIN.

clock.punch.note: Technical; techs will not use this word. Keep it in owner/audit screens only.

ticket.ticket.note: Salon slang mixes 'ticket' (English) and 'phiếu'; 'bill' also heard. Use 'Phiếu' on labels and accept 'ticket' in search.

ticket.tickets.note: Vietnamese has no plural marker; context carries it.

ticket.price.note: Standard. 'Tiền' (money) is what people say but 'Giá' is clearer as a column header.

ticket.card_tip.note: 'Tip' is always said in English; 'tiền tip' when spelled out. 'Tiền boa' is formal/Vietnam usage and sounds odd in a US salon. 'Thẻ' = card.

ticket.cash_tip.note: Spoken 'tip cash' or 'tip tiền mặt'; 'Tip mặt' is the short header form. Keep card and cash tips on separate lines always.

ticket.technician.note: 'Thợ' (worker/tech) is the universal word; 'kỹ thuật viên' is formal and never used in salons.

ticket.import_csv.note: 'File' is said in English; 'tập tin' is formal and rare.

ticket.import_from.note: System names (Square, Vagaro, Fresha) stay in English.

ticket.duplicate.note: 'Trùng' (duplicated/overlapping) is the natural word; 'Bản sao' means a copy you make on purpose.

ticket.void.note: 'Void' is said in English at the POS; 'Hủy phiếu' makes the object explicit.

ticket.reason.note: Required on every void or edit.

ticket.turn.note: Salon slang keeps the English word ('tới turn ai?', 'nửa turn'). Formal 'lượt' is understood but nobody says it. Do not translate.

ticket.half_turn.note: A small service (polish change, kids) counts as half a turn in many rotations.

ticket.walk_in.note: English loanword; 'khách vãng lai' is formal.

pay.pay_run.note: No salon slang for this; 'tính lương' (do payroll) is the verb people use. Button: 'Tính lương tuần này'.

pay.run_payroll.note: 'Tính lương' = compute pay. This is the owner's phrase for payroll night.

pay.workweek.note: Formal but clear; owners also just say 'tuần'.

pay.hours.note: 'Giờ' alone can mean time of day; 'Giờ làm' is unambiguous.

pay.overtime_hours.note: 'Overtime' is said in English by nearly everyone; 'giờ phụ trội' is the formal term used in Vietnamese-language legal articles. Show 'Giờ overtime (phụ trội)' once on the statement, then 'overtime'.

pay.day_rate.note: Standard; 'bao ngày' is also heard for a per-day guarantee.

pay.guarantee.note: Core salon term: the owner 'bao' (covers/guarantees) a weekly amount, e.g. 'bao $900/tuần'. A tech on this basis is 'thợ bao lương'. Formal Vietnamese would say 'lương cố định' but nobody in a salon does.

pay.commission.note: Salon term; literally 'eat-split'. Formal 'hoa hồng' (commission) is understood and used in articles, but 'ăn chia' is what owners and techs say. A tech on this basis is 'thợ ăn chia'.

pay.commission_rate.note: Always spoken as tech/owner fractions: '6/4' = tech 60%, '5/5' = 50/50. Show both the fraction and the percent: '6/4 (thợ 60%)'.

pay.split_6_4.note: The most common split; the first number is always the tech's share in US salons.

pay.regular_rate.note: A legal term (FLSA regular rate) with no salon equivalent; the gloss means 'actual hourly rate'. Add a one-line explainer.

pay.overtime_premium.note: The extra half-time owed, not the full 1.5x. Explain: 'phần 0.5 cộng thêm cho giờ trên 40'.

pay.minimum_wage_topup.note: 'Bù' = top up/make up the difference; 'lương tối thiểu' is standard. Owners will recognise 'bù' from 'bù tiền'.

pay.tips.vi: Tiền tip (của thợ, không tính vào lương)
pay.tips.note: State the 100%-to-tech rule explicitly on the statement.

pay.deductions.note: Standard. Note: this app does not compute tax withholding; use for owner-recorded advances ('ứng trước').

pay.advance.note: Techs often 'ứng' (draw) cash midweek; it shows as a deduction on payday.

pay.approve.note: Standard; 'OK' also acceptable on a small button.

pay.paid_by_check.note: Always said in English; formal 'chi phiếu' / 'ngân phiếu' is never used in salons. Keep 'Check'.

pay.paid_by_payroll.note: 'Payroll' as a loanword means the formal payroll service.

pay.check_cash_split.note: The habitual split of a week's pay between a check and cash. The app records the amounts; it does not advise on it.

pay.overtime_owed_unpaid.note: 'Nợ' (owed) is blunt on purpose; the dashboard red number.

pay.pay_basis.note: Literally 'way of computing pay'; clearer than 'cơ sở lương'.

stmt.pay_statement.note: 'Bảng lương' is universal; 'phiếu lương' is the formal pay-slip term and also fine. Techs say 'cái check' for the physical paycheck, so keep 'Bảng lương' for the document.

stmt.employer.vi: Chủ tiệm (người sử dụng lao động)
stmt.employer.note: Legal label first time; 'Chủ tiệm' thereafter.

stmt.employee.note: Techs say 'thợ'; 'nhân viên' is the legal word for employee and signals W-2 status.

stmt.your_tickets.note: The list the tech reconciles against their own notebook (sổ tay) or phone note.

stmt.questions_ask_employer.vi: Có thắc mắc? Hỏi chủ tiệm.

stmt.edited_tickets_note.en: Tickets marked * were edited or voided; see edit history.
stmt.edited_tickets_note.vi: Phiếu có dấu * đã được sửa hoặc hủy; xem lịch sử sửa.

audit.audit_binder.vi: Hồ sơ kiểm tra lao động
audit.audit_binder.note: No slang; owners say 'hồ sơ' (records) or 'giấy tờ' (papers) and 'bị DOL kiểm tra' / 'bị thanh tra' for the audit. 'Hồ sơ' is the right register.

audit.date_range.note: 'Từ ngày ... đến ngày ...' is the natural spoken form; use it for the two fields.

audit.who.note: 'Who edited'; a bare 'Ai' reads oddly as a column header.

audit.retention_note.en: Records are kept for at least 3 years.
audit.retention_note.vi: Hồ sơ được lưu ít nhất 3 năm.

audit.tip_report_monthly.vi: Báo cáo tip hàng tháng (từng thợ)
audit.tip_report_monthly.note: Stands in for the employee tip report; do not reference Form 8027 (food/beverage only).

settings.pay_basis_guarantee_or_commissi.en: Guarantee or commission, whichever is higher
settings.pay_basis_guarantee_or_commissi.vi: Bao lương hoặc ăn chia, bên nào cao hơn
settings.pay_basis_guarantee_or_commissi.note: The most common real arrangement ('bao $900, làm hơn thì ăn chia').

settings.pay_basis_day_rate_plus_commiss.note: Also common; must still be checked against hours.

settings.worker_status.note: Values: 'W-2 employee' -> 'Nhân viên W-2', '1099 contractor' -> 'Thợ 1099 (tự khai thuế)'. Keep the form numbers; everyone knows 'W-2' and '1099'.

settings.workweek_starts_on.vi: Tuần làm việc bắt đầu từ
settings.workweek_starts_on.note: Default Monday ('Thứ Hai'); many salons pay for Mon-Sun.

settings.language.note: Per-person setting; statement language can differ from tablet language.

settings.salon_name.note: 'Tiệm' (shop) is the universal word; 'salon' is also used as-is.

svc.manicure.note: Salon slang: 'làm tay' (do hands). 'Manicure' / 'mani' also said in English. Formal 'làm móng tay' is longer.

svc.acrylic_full_set.note: 'Bột' (powder) = acrylic in salon slang; 'full set' stays English. 'Đắp bột' = to apply acrylic.

svc.fill.note: Said in English ('fill bột'); 'dặm' is the older Vietnamese salon word, still heard.

svc.dip_powder.note: 'Dip' is the common spoken word; 'nhúng' = to dip.

svc.sns.note: Brand name used generically for dip powder; keep as-is.

svc.builder_gel.note: 'Đắp' = build up; many just say 'builder gel' or 'BIAB'.

svc.nail_art.note: 'Vẽ' (draw/paint); 'design' also said in English per nail ('design 2 ngón').

svc.french_tips.note: Just 'French' in salons; 'kiểu Pháp' is never used.

svc.removal.note: 'Tháo bột' / 'tháo gel' = remove acrylic/gel. 'Take off' also said in English.

svc.polish_change.note: 'Sơn' = polish (verb); 'thay sơn' also fine. Often a half turn.

svc.eyebrow_wax.note: 'Wax' stays English; 'chân mày' (Southern) vs 'lông mày' (Northern). Use 'chân mày'.

svc.kids.note: Kids mani/pedi; 'con nít' is spoken Southern slang, 'trẻ em' is the neutral label.

svc.callus.note: 'Chà gót' (scrub heels) is the salon term; formal 'tẩy da chết gót chân' is too long.

day.mon.note: Thứ Hai. Vietnamese weekdays are ordinal: Monday is 'second day'. 'T2' is the universal abbreviation.

day.sun.note: Chủ Nhật. Capitalise 'Chủ Nhật' when spelled out.

day.mon_long.note: Capitalise both words in UI labels; lower-case 'thứ hai' is also correct in running text.

month.jan.note: Tháng 1 / Tháng Một. Months are numbered in Vietnamese; 'Th1' or 'T1' both seen. Use 'Th' to avoid clashing with weekday 'T2'.

month.apr.note: Tháng 4. Note 'Tháng Tư' (not 'Tháng Bốn') when spelled out.

month.dec.note: Tháng 12. Full date in prose: 'ngày 7 tháng 10, 2026'; in tables keep US '10/07/2026'.

fmt.currency_example.note: Keep US format in the Vietnamese UI. Do NOT switch to vi-VN '1.234,56 đ'; US salon users read US money formats.

fmt.date_example.note: MM/DD/YYYY in both languages; spell the month ('7 Th10') where the order could confuse.

fmt.time_example.note: 12-hour clock; 'sáng' (morning) / 'chiều' (afternoon) / 'tối' (evening) replace AM/PM in Vietnamese. '9:30 AM' is also understood.
